title: Iurify Case Canvas
description: Graph representation of a legal case theory. Nodes are legal elements (facts, evidence, legal norms, case law); edges are typed legal relationships between them. Referential integrity (edge.source/edge.target must reference existing node ids), id uniqueness and absence of self-loops cannot be expressed in JSON Schema and are enforced by the backend (error code CANVAS_INTEGRITY_VIOLATION).

Uuid.description: RFC 9562 UUID. The pattern guarantees validation even when the validator treats 'format' as an annotation only.

NodeType.description: FACT: an alleged or proven event. EVIDENCE: a means of proof. LAW: a statutory/regulatory norm. JURISPRUDENCE: a judicial precedent or case-law criterion.

RelationshipType.description: SUPPORTS: source strengthens target (typically EVIDENCE -> FACT). CONTRADICTS: source weakens or is incompatible with target. DERIVES_FROM: source is inferred from target (fact chains, presumptions). APPLIES_TO: a norm or precedent governs a fact (LAW|JURISPRUDENCE -> FACT). INTERPRETS: a precedent interprets a norm (JURISPRUDENCE -> LAW). Type-pair conventions are guidance; atypical pairs are flagged by the AI audit, not rejected.

Origin.description: Who created the element. AI_GENERATED elements come from narrative processing; USER_CREATED elements come from manual canvas edits.

Position.description: Top-left anchor of the node in logical (device-independent) canvas units. Bounded to keep rendering numerically safe.

userModified.description: True when a lawyer changed type, title or content of the node after creation. Position changes do not set this flag (layout is not legal content). AI re-processing must never overwrite nodes where origin = USER_CREATED or userModified = true.
True when a lawyer changed the relationshipType of an AI-generated edge.
